checks.title: What we check
checks.intro: Seven areas and more than 20 checkpoints. We go through the site like a customer: home page, product pages, checkout, withdrawal flow and terms.

items.title: The withdrawal button
items.body: Since 19 June 2026 customers must be able to withdraw from a purchase directly on the site. You must have a clearly labelled withdrawal function with a confirmation step, and the customer must get an acknowledgement straight away.

items.title: Prices and discounts
items.body: When you reduce a price, you must show the lowest price from the last 30 days and calculate the discount from it. The total price, with delivery and fees, must be visible before the customer orders.

items.title: The cookie banner
items.body: Rejecting cookies must be as easy as accepting them, on the first screen. No choices may be pre-ticked.

items.title: Misleading design
items.body: You may not use false urgency such as "only 2 left", pre-ticked extras, fees that appear only at the last step, or "no thanks" buttons that make the customer feel guilty.

items.title: Subscriptions
items.body: You must show clearly when a free trial becomes paid, what it costs and how the customer cancels. We also compare how easy it is to cancel with how easy it is to sign up.

items.title: Accessibility
items.body: Since 28 June 2025 online shops must be usable by everyone, whatever their abilities. You must also publish information on how the site meets the requirements. We test the site against WCAG 2.1 AA.

items.title: Environmental claims
items.body: From 27 September 2026 you may not call a product "eco-friendly", "green" or similar without a recognised ecolabel, such as the Nordic Swan or the EU Ecolabel. Nor may you call a product climate neutral because you offset emissions. We find such claims on the site.

items.title: Reviews and company details
items.body: If you show customer reviews, you must say whether and how you check that they come from real customers. Company name, company registration number, address and email must be easy to find.

items.title: Digital Fairness Act
items.body: The European Commission presented the proposal on 11 November 2026. It is not law yet. We show what on your site would need to change if it is adopted, so you have time to prepare.

steps.title: We go through your site like a customer
steps.body: Automatic tests and a walk-through of the whole buying flow, from the home page to the checkout. Every finding is tied to a specific consumer-law rule.

steps.title: You know exactly what to change
steps.body: For each issue: what is wrong, which rule applies, how serious it is and how to fix it. With a screenshot as evidence.

compare.title: Free check or monitoring?
compare.intro: The free check shows where your shop stands today. Sites and rules change all the time. With monitoring we check your shop every week and alert you when something needs fixing.

compare.risk: If a shop breaks consumer law, a court can, at the request of the Swedish Consumer Ombudsman, impose a penalty of up to four percent of turnover.

items.a: No. {name} checks online shops against consumer law and shows where a site falls short. The results do not replace legal advice on a specific case.

items.q: Do you need access to our systems?
items.a: No. We only look at what an ordinary customer sees on your site.

items.q: Can I request a check of someone else's website?
items.a: No. The free results are only sent to people who own or work for the website. We check this before sending.

items.q: Why do you ask for a test order?
items.a: The withdrawal button and its confirmation often only appear after a purchase. You get the results within 24 hours either way. If you place a test order and send us the order number, we check the whole flow and send an addendum within 24 hours.

items.q: What do you do in the checkout?
items.a: Only if you choose it when you request the check: we put an item in the cart and fill in {name}'s own company details up to payment, to see add-ons, the total price and the wording of the order button. We never press that button and never enter card details or anyone else's personal data. Without your permission we stop at the first step of the checkout.

items.q: What happens to my email address?
items.a: It is used for the results and one follow-up. Data is stored in the EU. You can ask us to delete it any time.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.draftNotice: Draft – to be reviewed by a lawyer before launch.

sections.heading: Who is responsible for your data
sections.body: The data controller is {company}, reg. no. {orgNr}, {address}.

sections.heading: What we collect
sections.body: When you request a free check, we store the website you enter, your email address, the language you chose, whether you allowed us to go through the checkout, whether you plan to place a test order, and the time. When you enter a web address, we also run an automatic instant check of the site's home page on our own server in Sweden. The address and the result are kept for at most two hours and are not linked to you. If you send a message through the contact form, we store the topic, your email address, the domain and the message if you give them, and the time.

sections.heading: Why, and on what legal basis
sections.body: We use the details to prepare and send the results, to answer your messages and for one follow-up. The legal basis is your consent, which you can withdraw at any time.

sections.heading: Where the data is stored and for how long
sections.body: The data is stored with our form provider inside the EU. We delete it no later than 12 months after the results are sent or we have replied to you, or earlier if you ask us to.

sections.heading: Cookies and visitor statistics
sections.body: The website uses no cookies and no advertising tracking. We count visits with GoatCounter, which we run on our own server in Sweden. It stores no IP address and nothing that can be linked to you, only which pages and steps are shown, which page the visitor came from, approximate country and type of browser and screen.

sections.heading: Your rights
sections.body: You have the right to access, correct and delete your data, and to complain to the Swedish Authority for Privacy Protection (IMY).
